Medical Appointment Scheduling

A Full Schedule Is Only Useful If Patients Actually Show Up

Appointment scheduling looks simple from the outside, book a time, send a reminder, done. In practice, it's a constant balancing act: fitting new patients in around existing ones, managing provider availability across multiple locations, filling cancellations before they become empty slots, and getting patients to actually show up once they're booked.

No-shows cost more than the lost visit. They break the day's flow, waste staff time, and leave a slot that could have gone to another patient sitting empty. Most no-shows aren't intentional, they happen because a reminder call never got through, or rescheduling felt like more hassle than it was worth.

This is handled by the same PMEX virtual front desk team that answers your calls, not by a standalone automated system. A real person books the visit, calls to confirm it, and works the waitlist when a slot opens up, all within your existing scheduling system.
